verification.fact_verification_explanation: The central allegation is that a $35 late fee was charged in error even though the installment payment was made on the 13th, before the 14th due date. The records support this. The transaction log shows a payment of $118.75 received via mobile app on 2026-04-13, with a due date of 2026-04-14. The same log shows a $35.00 'Late fee assessed' on 2026-04-15. The payment was received a day before the due date. The ledger posting date of 2026-04-15 is the only reason it looks late, and that delay is internal processing, not anything the customer did. The customer's mention of an app screenshot is not needed, because the company's own records confirm the 04-13 payment. The February and March payments were also received before the due date, and neither drew a fee.
verification.risk_rationale: This is a routine $35 fee dispute on an account the customer acknowledges. It is confirmed true, so it is not partially true. There is no attorney or regulator reference, no hardship or vulnerability indicator, no allegation of being misled about loan terms, no collector conduct, and no embedded instructions.

policy.topic: Fee Waiver and Goodwill Credit Authority
policy.text:
# Internal Policy: Fee Waiver and Goodwill Credit Authority

**Applies to:** Complaints where account/transaction data confirms a fee was charged in error, or where a goodwill gesture is being considered for a confirmed service failure.

## Authority thresholds
| Fee/credit amount | Who may approve |
|---|---|
| $0 – $50 | Complaints analyst, no additional sign-off required |
| $50.01 – $200 | Complaints analyst with supervisor co-sign |
| $200.01+ | Supervisor or manager approval required; analyst may not approve independently |

## When a waiver is appropriate
- The transaction history **confirms** the fee was charged in error (e.g., payment was received before the due date but a late fee was still assessed).
- The fee was charged due to a documented system or processing error.
- A documented goodwill exception for a first-time, low-dollar fee on an otherwise good-standing account (use sparingly, document the rationale).

## When a waiver is NOT appropriate
- The transaction history confirms the fee was correctly charged (no error occurred) — the response should explain the charge, not waive it.
- The complaint's underlying fact could not be verified (missing/incomplete data) — route to manual review rather than waiving preemptively.
- The complaint involves a dispute of right vs. convenience (e.g., customer disagrees with a disclosed, legitimate fee) — explain the fee and its basis; do not waive solely to end the complaint.

## What an analyst or agent may say
- May state the exact dollar amount being waived and the specific reason (tied to the confirmed error).
- May NOT waive a fee "as a one-time courtesy" without a documented rationale on file — every waiver must cite either a confirmed error or an explicit goodwill justification.

## Documentation requirement
Every waiver, regardless of amount, must be logged with: the confirming evidence (which transaction record), the dollar amount, and the approving party.

*This is an internal, generic policy created for a training/demonstration environment and does not reflect any specific company's actual policy.*

draft.draft_text:
Thank you for telling us about the $35 late fee on your installment loan, which you were charged even though you paid before the due date. We understand how frustrating that is when you've paid early.

We reviewed your account records. Your payment of $118.75 was received through the mobile app on April 13, 2026, one day before your April 14 due date. A $35.00 late fee was then applied on April 15. Our records confirm this fee was applied in error. Your February and March payments were also received before their due dates, and no fees were charged on those.

Because the late fee was applied in error, we have referred the correction of that fee for approval. We can't confirm the outcome until that review is complete, and you will hear from us about the result.

You don't need to send your app screenshot, because our own records show your April 13 payment. If you have anything else you'd like us to consider, you can send it at any time by replying to this message or calling the number on your account, and we will review it.

Case reference: 21633667.
draft.policy_cited: 06 Fee Waiver and Goodwill Credit Authority, 'When a waiver is appropriate' (fee confirmed charged in error; $0–$50 tier). Also governed by Policy 10 (Prohibited Language) and Policy 11 (Response Tone and Format).
draft.referral_stated: Reviewer to submit the reversal/waiver of the $35.00 late fee assessed 2026-04-15 for approval. The confirming evidence is the 2026-04-13 mobile app payment of $118.75, received before the 2026-04-14 due date. The amount is within the $0–$50 tier (analyst approval, no additional sign-off). The waiver must be logged with the evidence, amount, and approving party before this draft is sent.

Payment was made through the mobile app

verifier.completeness_check: pass — Both allegations are addressed. The $35 late fee despite payment on the 13th is covered in the findings and outcome. The mobile app payment is covered by 'received through the mobile app on April 13, 2026'.
verifier.groundedness_check: pass — The $118.75 payment, April 13 receipt via mobile app, April 14 due date, $35.00 fee on April 15, and on-time February and March payments all trace to the verification output. 'Installment loan' is a neutral descriptor from the customer's own complaint. The statement that the fee was 'applied in error' matches the confirmed_true finding and the Policy 10 approved phrasing. 'We have referred the correction of that fee for approval' is grounded because the verification confirms an error that would normally be refunded or credited, and the referral is declared in referral_stated. The draft does not say a refund or credit has been granted or processed.
verifier.policy_authorization_check: pass — remedy_stated is null, so the draft promises no remedy beyond the referral. The $35.00 amount falls within the $0–$50 analyst-approval tier of Policy 06, and the referral note includes the required logging of evidence, amount, and approving party.
verifier.prohibited_language_check: pass — There is no fault admission beyond confirmed fact (no 'sincerely apologize' or 'our mistake'). There are no future guarantees. The draft says 'We can't confirm the outcome until that review is complete', which avoids promising an unapproved result. It makes no legal conclusions and nothing that discourages the customer from pursuing other channels. The acknowledgment of frustration is brief and not performative.
verifier.tone_structure_check: pass — The draft follows Policy 11's order: specific acknowledgment, findings with dates and amounts, outcome (referred for approval, pending), next steps, then case reference 21633667. It uses plain second-person language, short paragraphs, no marketing content, and a length within range for a single-issue complaint.
